text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.5% today to $422.33, capping a dramatic two-day surge of over 7.5% since September 30th. The sharp move up follows the G7's announcement to release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months—a supply injection that might seem bearish for a refiner, but instead appears to have reassured markets that diesel shortages won't spiral further, reducing the risk of demand destruction and supporting refining margins. With refineries already running at 92.5% capacity and diesel inventories tight, the coordinated reserve release signals policy support for fuel availability rather than a flood that would crater prices.

The broader context shows tension between supply concerns and geopolitical risks that keep oil prices elevated. U.S. crude sits at $96/barrel while global crude trades at $114/barrel—a significant spread driven by supply disruptions in the Middle East and Europe. Even as the G7 releases reserves to ease diesel pressure, the threat of renewed Iran strikes and ongoing Middle East instability keeps crude prices supported, which can benefit refining profitability when crude and product prices move together.
